newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh's Hasina rekindles independence memory.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh's Hasina rekindles independence memory.

text.p: Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina on Friday rekindled memories of the independence war that her father waged 25 years ago by lighting a torch that will be sent around the country.

"Bear it (the torch) in your hands and reflect the light on your memories. I believe you have all fondly preserved the unforgettable moments of our liberation struggle and recall the enormous sacrifices we made," Hasina told an estimated 25,000 people at the inauguration of the torch rally at Dhaka's Suhrawardy Uddyan (park).

On the same site on March 7, 1971, Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, then chief of Awami League, gave final directives to the people of then East Pakistan (now Bangladesh) to prepare for the independence war against Pakistan.
"You must now get ready with whatever you have...stop paying taxes and start defying orders from the Pakistani junta," Mujib said in a speech to over one million people.
"This is our struggle for independence...and we will wrest it, Inshallah," he said.
As Hasina, Mujib's daughter, handed the torch to two heroes of the 1971 war, the crowd and chanted Joy Bangla (Long Live Bangladesh) and Joy Bangabandhu, as they reveredly refer to Mujib.
The torch will be sent through 64 administrative districts before returning to Dhaka on March 26, the anniversary of Bangladesh's independence.
"I urge you to use your indomitable spirit and energy now for building Sonar Bangla (golden Bangladesh), the dream of Bangabandhu," Hasina said.
Hasina said on Friday "my heart still bleeds...and I can share the pains of millions of others who had lost their near and dear ones in the independence war."
She was briefly referring to Mujib's killing in a 1975 army coup, along with his wife, three sons and many other relatives.
Hasina and her only sister, Sheikh Rehana, were both travelling abroad at the time of the coup.

Since taking power after a landmark general election in June, Hasina has ordered the trial of those accused of killing Mujib. Six of the accused, now in police custody, will appear in court next week.
